summary: This is a sound, low-risk port of the sibling's proven paired-path launch cleanup onto glue that the current master profile (9dcaec316b3045a7) shows is still there on every full batch>1 shape. The expected effect is about +1-2.5% on those four shapes but only about +0.4% on the headline geomean, inside the CI, so it has to be judged per shape and per kernel row, not on the headline. No companion is needed.
justification: Mechanism checks out. In master kernel_fn (submission.py lines 353-399) the paired path runs torch.zeros(q_attn), two strided cast-copies, torch.empty plus two un-pad copies, and then FusedRMSNormGate. The current master profile shows the copies as elementwise_kernel<128,4> x3 plus x2: 6.2+4.4 us at full decode_16, 6.7+4.8 at decode_32, 7.0+4.8 at verify_16, and 7.0 x3 plus a second row below the top-12 at verify_32. The zero-fill and the norm-gate fall in the '... more' tail, about 2-3 us each. Replacing them with two one-program-per-(token, head) Triton kernels that each move 128-256 B per program should cost about 2-4 us total, so about 8-12 us saved per full batch>1 shape. Against current master totals (364.9/535.8/603.9/932.9 us, not the stale 407/544/587/907 the hypothesis quotes from fb07a3bd) that is about +2.5%/+1.7%/+1.5%/+1.1%, consistent with the stated directions. decode_1/verify_1 (unpaired, batch 1) and every sliding shape run identical code, so flat there is a genuine control. Weakest link: magnitude against the scoring. Full shapes carry weight 16 against 46 for sliding in each load, so the load-level gains are about 0.9% (decode_16), 0.7% (decode_32), 0.5% (verify_16) and 0.4% (verify_32). That makes about +0.4% geomean over the six loads, well inside the current CI half-width (about 1.5%). The scored result will almost certainly classify neutral or within-ci, and its evidence is the elementwise_kernel<128,4> rows vanishing plus the two new kernels' own us in top_kernels. The second weakest link is that the sibling's +3.8-6.4% came from an attention-only problem with much smaller per-shape totals, where the pad was also fused into a pre-attention kernel. Its percentages do not transfer; only the absolute us do. Correctness: the epilogue is verbatim from a kernel that passed muse_attention_decode's tests, and its gate offset (Hq+2*Hkv)*64 + h*64 with qkv.stride(0) matches master's gate = qkv[:, hq*d+2*hkv*d:]. Its fp32 scaleless RMSNorm (eps 1e-5) times sigmoid(gate) matches FusedRMSNormGate(MuseSpark1xRMSNorm(64, has_weight=False)) up to bf16 rounding order, far inside the 3-15% bound. The pad kernel's bf16 to E4M3 cast is round-to-nearest in both torch and Triton; Triton saturates and torch does not, but post-QK-norm q magnitudes (at most about 8 times the norm weight) are far below 448, so the two cast paths should match bit for bit. The one real hazard is FusedQKNorm's q layout. The kernel must index q through its real strides (q.stride(0), and the head stride if q is 3-D), not assume [T, 1024] contiguous. Master's q.view(tokens, s, 2, g, d) proves only that the last two dims are dense.
confounders: fa3-hdim128-head-pairing-batched (depends_on): this change exists only on the paired path that hypothesis added, so it cannot be measured without it, and an ab-revert would delete the code under test. The interaction is by construction, not a confounder. A gain is attributable to removing that hypothesis's glue, read directly from the elementwise rows.

post-expert-norm-triton-small-t: different area (MoE combine) and gated at T<32, so it does not touch the attention glue. It changes only the decode_16 totals that the percentages are computed against. No confounding.

marlin-block-m-cap-16 and sglang-pipeline-parity-router-hilo-m8: different areas (Marlin MoE GEMMs and router GEMM) with no shared launches or buffers with the q pad or o un-pad. No confounding beyond run-to-run drift on the totals.
interference: No companion is warranted. An ab-revert of the pairing is meaningless because it removes the code path being changed. An ab-tune of the pairing gate (for example batch>1 versus some other gate) does not affect what this hypothesis measures on the shapes where pairing is on. A control splitting sub-change (1), the epilogue, from (2), the pad kernel, is unnecessary, because the profile names both new kernels (_paired_norm_gate_kernel, _pair_pad_q_kernel) and the removed elementwise rows per shape. Either a gain or a loss can therefore be attributed to the sub-change responsible from the single run's top_kernels. The ambiguity this result does carry is statistical: the headline effect is below the CI, and a second run would not fix that. Read the per-shape us on the four full batch>1 shapes against the flat controls (sliding, full decode_1/verify_1) in the same run.
rules_flags: None blocking. The query is still rounded to FP8 E4M3 and no coarser (rule allows exactly this); the zero half is exact FP8 0, so every logit is unchanged and every key is still attended. The output stays BF16 into the o GEMM.

Graph safety: both kernels must take tokens/hq/hkv/G from cfg/shape only (constexpr or grid), with no .item() and no branching on tensor values. The output buffers are fresh per call (torch.empty), and nothing derived from data is cached in state.
Do not keep a persistent pre-zeroed q buffer in state to skip the zero writes. The hypothesis correctly has the kernel write the zero half every call.
open_questions: What is FusedQKNorm's q return: a fresh contiguous [T, 16, 64] tensor or a strided view of qkv? The pad kernel must take both the token and head strides. Implement it as reading q[t, h, j] through q.stride(0) and q.stride(-2) (or q.view(tokens, hq, d).stride()), and assert the last-dim stride is 1.

FA3's paired output is [tokens, hq, 128] bf16. Pass out.stride(0) and out.stride(1), as the sibling does, rather than assuming contiguity; on varlen verify the output can be [T, H, D] from a [B, L, ...] view.

Given about +0.4% expected geomean and a scored submit, does the operator accept that the classification will very likely be neutral/within-ci, so that promotion has to be by hand on per-shape evidence, as was done for paired-heads-launch-cleanup-ab-tune-batch-gate in DECISIONS?

Follow-up rather than blocker: the unpaired path's q.view(...).to(FP8) and the k/v FP8 casts are still separate launches on every shape. Folding the k/v casts into _pair_pad_q_kernel would stack on cache-store-fused-fp8-cast's open follow-up, but keep this run's scope as written for attribution.
